title: Payroll ladder and billing-offset scan — May 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick spreadsheet-style scan to test payroll ladder adjustments vs. billing (token price) sensitivity and regional GPU mix FX effects. Goal: surface small changes in hiring phasing or marginal price to see near-term runway delta and break-even thresholds for Q3–Q4 2026. This is a working sheet — assumptions listed, formulas simplified.

Assumptions (high level):
- Baseline token price = $0.0025 per token (hosted API blended rate; unit here is $/1k tokens where applicable).
- Average fully-loaded FY26 engineering comp per FTE (incl benefits, equity accrual, payroll tax) = $220k/year (~$18.3k/month).
- Ops/SRE/Platform avg = $180k/year. Sales/CS avg = $160k/year. Hiring phasing uses ramp% over first 3 months for new hires (50% / 75% / 100%).
- GPU spend modeled as monthly cost buckets by region (NA, EU, APAC) with blended cost per GPU-hour and utilization conversion to $/month. FX adjustments applied to EU and APAC buckets (-3% and +5% respectively to reflect currency expectations).
- Revenue is simplified: billed tokens * token price = token revenue. We model three token demand scenarios (Base, Surge, Drop).

Summary table (monthly, simplified) — columns: Month | New FTEs | Total FTEs | Payroll ($k) | GPU cost ($k) | Token volume (1k tokens) | Token price ($/1k) | Token revenue ($k) | Unit margin ($k)
Rows: Q3 2026 monthly snapshot (Jul, Aug, Sep) under Baseline, Upside (+10% price), Downside (-15% price).

Month,New FTEs,Total FTEs,Payroll_k,GPU_cost_k,Token_vol_1k,Token_price_per1k,Token_revenue_k,Unit_margin_k

Key calculated lines (how to read):
- Payroll_k = sum(FTEs * weighted avg comp / 12). Simplified above to show monthly fully-loaded payroll in thousands.
- GPU_cost_k = modeled regional GPU pool cost + burst capacity buffer (rounded).
- Token_revenue_k = Token_vol_1k * Token_price_per1k / 1000 (but values scaled to k for the table).
- Unit_margin_k = Token_revenue_k - (Payroll_k + GPU_cost_k + other opex buffer 15% of payroll). Negative indicates cash burn contribution.

Break-even sensitivity (one-line):
- For Jul baseline volume (420M tokens / 420,000 1k units) payroll+gpu+opex = 2776 + 560 + 0.15*2776 = 2776 + 560 + 416.4 = 3752.4k total cost. Required token price to breakeven = total_cost / token_vol_1k = 3752.4 / 420000 = 0.00893 ($/1k) -> $0.00893 per 1k tokens (approx $8.93 per million tokens).
- Current baseline price (0.0025) is well below the breakeven; shows we rely on other revenue or different accounting (this sheet intentionally isolates hosted token economics to be conservative).

Regional GPU mix/FX sensitivity (notes):
- Baseline GPU split: NA 60% (higher $/hour), EU 30% (apply -3% FX benefit), APAC 10% (apply +5% FX pressure).
- Small shifts in NA->EU (10% shift) reduce GPU cost by ~6% across the bucket; shift to APAC increases cost ~4%.
- We model a scenario where we migrate 15% workload to cheaper EU preemptible pools (subject to latency SLA checks): immediate monthly GPU_k reduction ~ $34k but risk-adjusted expected impact on support ops is +$12k (net saving ~$22k).

Hiring phasing experiments (quick):
- Option A (frontload): hire 10 FTEs now (Jul ramp applied) -> payroll shock +$183k/mo in Q3, expected product velocity improves token retention by +4% leading to +16.8k 1k token units (very optimistic). Net runway delta minimal unless price moves up.
- Option B (deferred): hire 10 FTEs starting Oct (push to Q4) -> payroll uplift deferred, but risk of slower product velocity and potential lost revenue.
- We recommend a compromise: 6 hires Jul, 4 hires Oct (phased) with canary testing on EU preemptible migration to validate latency SLA before wider shift.

Action items / decisions needed:
1) Confirm whether hosted token price can be experimented with in a small cohort (we need legal/pm approval). If yes, run a +10% price A/B test for new signups starting Aug for 6 weeks.
2) Approve a pilot to move 15% of non-latency-sensitive workload to EU preemptible pool — coordinate infra (PRI: SRE).
3) Defer 40% of planned Q3 hiring to Oct unless the +10% price test shows no drop in conversion.
4) Finance to produce an adjusted P&L that layers in enterprise committed revenue (which isn't in the isolated token model here).

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Sales credits / coupons heavily distort effective token price for new customers — need to incorporate net effective price weighting across customer cohorts.
- Latency-sensitive customers may not tolerate EU preemptible; need trial coverage and rollback automation.
- FX movements could vary more widely; sheet uses conservative small adjustments.

Short next steps (owner: Samira):
- Clean numbers with SRE on estimated GPU cost delta (due 2026-05-18).
- Finance to crosswalk with ARR bookings and committed capacity (due 2026-05-20).
- PM/Legal to sign off on A/B price experiment scope and safety rails (due 2026-05-21).

Notes on provenance / linked tickets:
- See JIRA-PRICING-94 for price experiment scoping.
- See GH PR linked above for the GPU cost projection script (WIP).

Quick sensitivity summary (one paragraph):
Small moves in token price have outsized effects on short-term hosted-margin because payroll is relatively fixed in the near-term. Moving modest volume to cheaper regional GPU capacity delivers tactical savings but introduces operational risk. A cautious hiring cadence combined with a small price experiment and a targeted EU preemptible pilot gives the best risk-adjusted path to improve run-rate without a large one-time payroll shock.

Sheet provenance: working spreadsheet exported to doc format for review. Keep as draft until SRE/Finance checks are in.
